text:
sarah: Heads-up — ran the nightly fused vs paged attention sweep on llama-13b with the new kernel_selector heuristics. Seeing a regresssion for small-batch low-latency cases when using interleaved KV layout. numbers below.

raj: ugh, details? how bad is it?

sarah: p99 latency (bs=1, seq=1024): flash_fused_v2 + interleaved = 82ms, paged_attention_v1 + separate = 68ms. ~21% regression. throughput at bs=8 down ~12%.

oliver: that's enough to bite latency SLOs. did you profile?

sarah: yes — nvprof + our tracing. hotpath shows extra global loads in kv_read when stride % 32 != 0. looks like bank conflicts + fallback memcpy in kernel for unaligned strides.

kevin: can you paste the stack/prof snippet?

sarah: 
```
# perf snapshot (condensed)
flash_fused_v2::attention_kernel  -- 48% (memory+ldg)
kv_read_unaligned               -- 22% (serial memcpy path)
warp_serialization_handler      -- 8%
compute_attn                    -- 16%
```

raj: what dtype? bf16 vs fp16? alignment matters more for 2-byte vs 4-byte lanes.

sarah: bf16 on these runs. interestingly, when forcing fp16 the memcpy path still shows but magnitude drops (less perf hit).

marie: so maybe our interleaved layout isn't enforcing a 128-byte alignment for kv pages, causing misaligned loads for ppl with certain strides. did the new kernel_selector change alignment assumptions?

sarah: yes, selector now prefers interleaved for fused kernels when avg_seq < 2048 to improve packing. but it forgot to set align_stride=128 for interleaved path.

perf-bot: CI attention-sweep (#19724) finished. regressions detected: flash_fused_v2 (bs=1, seq=1024) p99 +21%. See /ci/artifacts/19724/attention-sweep.json

oliver: repro locally with this quick bench:
```
./bench_attention --model llama-13b --kernel flash_fused_v2 --seq 1024 --bs 1 --dtype bf16 --kv interleaved --align 64
```
change --align 128 to compare.

kevin: quick mitigation: make kernel_selector set align_stride=128 for interleaved bf16, and add a runtime assert that stride % 64 == 0 for bf16 and % 128 == 0 for fp16? (or the other way around depending on bytes).

raj: careful: making asserts in hotpath will crash customers if layout mismatch; better to clamp/round-up stride at layout stage. also add a fallback flag to prefer separate layout when unaligned.

marie: propose steps: 1) revert heuristic that prefers interleaved for avg_seq < 2048, 2) add align fixup in kv_layout allocator, 3) add a selector unit test exercising bs=1/bs=8 mixed workloads.

oliver: agree. also add microbenchmark for different strides: 64/96/128/160 bytes to quantify bank-conflict cliff. aim to catch >5% p99 regression.

sarah: i'll push a short PR with the align fixup + test. PR will include a reproducer script.

kevin: if we can't land fast, workaround in runtime: prefer_paged=true forces paged_attention_v1 which avoids the memcpy. we can flip default in canary.

sarah: noted. I'll run canary with prefer_paged=true for the next deploy and post results.

perf-bot: canary run started: attention-canary-197246. Will report within 30m.

raj: low-effort extra check: add logging when kv_layout produces stride not multiple of 32 for bf16 so we can find impacted customers. low overhead.

marie: good call. also update release notes to mention alignment behavior and that interleaved layout may be disabled for tight-latency tiers until fixed.

sarah: PR: github.com/redwood-inference/serving/compare/kv-align-fix (WIP). repro + graphs attached in PR.

kevin: cool. once PR lands, run full sweep: bs=1/4/8 seq=512/1024/2048 dtype={bf16,fp16} kernels={flash_fused_v2,paged_attention_v1,flash_hybrid}. collect p50/p95/p99.

sarah: will do. update in ~45m. :hourglass_flowing_sand:

oliver: thanks — tagging platform-oncall so we don't surprise any customers. @platform-oncall

perf-bot: attention-canary-197246 finished: p99 (bs=1,seq=1024,interleaved) down to 70ms when align_stride enforced (vs 82ms before).
